decision.summary: Tenant reported a chirping hallway CO alarm; it is a sealed unit fitted in 2019 with a 7-year life, so it is past end of life. Treated as urgent, not a confirmed CO emergency. Logged JOB-101 and JOB-102 (fan), advised tenant on safety, asked landlord for approval.

answers.question: Is this a CO emergency, battery issue or end-of-life alarm?
answers.answer: Most likely end-of-life: single chirp about once a minute, no continuous alarm, no symptoms mentioned, sealed battery (so not a replaceable battery) and the unit is past its 7-year life (fitted 2019-04-02). Real CO is not ruled out, so safety advice was given and it is urgent; it becomes an emergency if the alarm sounds continuously or anyone has symptoms.

answers.question: Who is responsible?
answers.answer: The landlord, via us. Clause 12.8 makes the tenant replace batteries, but this is a sealed unit with no replaceable battery, so it is an equipment replacement. Clause 12.9 (tenant tests and reports promptly) was met. Clause 12.17 doesn't apply: the call wasn't avoidable or out of hours call-out.

answers.question: What actions and what told to tenant?
answers.answer: Created JOB-101 (urgent) and JOB-102 (routine fan), requested landlord approval (APR-104), scheduled follow-up for 12 Oct. Told tenant not to remove the battery, gave gas emergency 0800 111 999 and 999 advice, the 72h target and next update date.

conflicts: Call dropped mid-conversation, so the tenant's question about removing the battery was never answered live; answered by SMS

args.body: Hi Priya, sorry our call dropped. Please don't remove the battery or cover the alarm. Yours is a sealed unit that is now past its 7-year life, so a regular chirp usually means it needs replacing, and we're treating it as urgent. We've logged it and our target is to get it sorted within 72 hours. Replacing the alarm is for the landlord/us to arrange, not you. Safety: if the alarm sounds continuously, or anyone feels dizzy, has headaches, nausea or flu-like symptoms, leave the flat, open doors, call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (or 999 if anyone is unwell), and don't use the boiler until checked. We've also logged the noisy bathroom fan as a separate routine job. We'll update you by Monday 12 October.
